description.narrative:
Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene - To address the some of the WASH gaps, 3230 targeted households will benefit from the distribution of soap and bottles of liquid chlorine to make water safe for use. The response will also procure and distribute 50 x 20 litres of granular chlorine for disinfecting both toilets at the camps and surrounding public facilities. Further, 20 temporal latrines and bathing shelters to improve on the hygiene gaps. A targeted 46,533 (7,887 households both in the IDPs and surrounding villages) people will be reached with door-to-door hygiene messaging to promote good hygiene practices. In addition, 50 hygiene promoters in the camps will be trained to ensure adherence of minimum hygiene standards at household level and promote hand washing.
Food Security and Livelihoods – The food requirements for the next 45 days will include 58.14 metric tonnes of cereal with a standard ration of 400g per person per day. The quantity required for pulses is 17.44 metric tonnes at 120g per person per day, and 0.73 metric tonnes of salt at 5g per person per day. The project will conduct a distribution session to all the targeted affected households.
Protection – Some of the key intervention areas will include strengthening or formation of camp child protection structures (child protection committees, Case Care Workers (CCWs), information dissemination on child rights, and provision of game equipment to keep children occupied.
